claim: Ferritins are ubiquitous proteins that oxidise and store iron within a protein shell to protect cells from oxidative damage.
source: Ferritins are ubiquitous proteins that oxidise and store iron within a protein shell to protect cells from oxidative damage.
evidence: This is a general statement about ferritins supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: EncFtn has two main alpha helices.
source: We show that this encapsulated ferritin (EncFtn) has two main alpha helices
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data presented in the manuscript, including crystal structure analysis.

claim: EncFtn assembles in a metal dependent manner to form a ferroxidase center at a dimer interface.
source: which assemble in a metal dependent manner to form a ferroxidase center at a dimer interface
evidence: This is supported by experimental data including native PAGE, analytical gel-filtration, and native mass spectrometry showing metal-dependent assembly.

claim: EncFtn adopts an open decameric structure that is topologically distinct from other ferritins.
source: EncFtn adopts an open decameric structure that is topologically distinct from other ferritins.
evidence: This is supported by crystal structure data and SEC-MALLS analysis showing decameric assembly.

claim: EncFtn acts as a ferroxidase.
source: While EncFtn acts as a ferroxidase, it cannot mineralize iron.
evidence: This is supported by ferroxidase activity assays measuring Fe2+ to Fe3+ oxidation at 315 nm.

claim: EncFtn cannot mineralize iron.
source: While EncFtn acts as a ferroxidase, it cannot mineralize iron.
evidence: This is supported by TEM analysis showing irregular precipitates rather than controlled mineralization, and ferrozine assays showing limited iron binding capacity.

claim: The encapsulin shell associates with iron but is not enzymatically active.
source: Conversely, the encapsulin shell associates with iron, but is not enzymatically active
evidence: This is supported by ferroxidase assays showing no catalytic activity and ferrozine assays showing iron binding capacity of ~2200 iron ions.

claim: EncFtn must be housed within the encapsulin for iron storage.
source: we demonstrate that EncFtn must be housed within the encapsulin for iron storage
evidence: This is supported by TEM showing controlled mineralization only in EncFtn-Enc complexes and ferrozine assays showing the complex sequesters over 4100 iron ions.

claim: The encapsulin nanocompartment is widely distributed in bacteria and archaea.
source: This encapsulin nanocompartment is widely distributed in bacteria and archaea
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies identifying encapsulins in various bacterial and archaeal species.

claim: The encapsulin nanocompartment represents a distinct class of iron storage system where oxidation and mineralization of iron are distributed between two proteins.
source: represents a distinct class of iron storage system, where the oxidation and mineralization of iron are distributed between two proteins
evidence: This is supported by the combined biochemical and structural data showing EncFtn performs oxidation while encapsulin provides mineralization space.

claim: Encapsulin nanocompartments share a common architecture comprising an icosahedral shell formed by oligomeric assembly of encapsulin protein.
source: They share a common architecture, comprising an icosahedral shell formed by the oligomeric assembly of a protein, encapsulin
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous structural studies of encapsulins from different organisms.

claim: Encapsulin is structurally related to the HK97 bacteriophage capsid protein gp5.
source: that is structurally related to the HK97 bacteriophage capsid protein gp5
evidence: This is supported by citation to structural comparison studies.

claim: Pyrococcus furiosus and Myxococcus xanthus encapsulin shell-proteins form 32 nm icosahedra with 180 subunits.
source: both the Pyrococcus furiosus (Akita et al., 2007) and Myxococcus xanthus (McHugh et al., 2014) encapsulin shell-proteins form 32 nm icosahedra with 180 subunits
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous structural characterization studies.

claim: Thermotoga maritima encapsulin forms a 25 nm, 60-subunit icosahedron.
source: while the Thermotoga maritima (Sutter et al., 2008) encapsulin is smaller still with a 25 nm, 60-subunit icosahedron
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous structural characterization.

claim: Encapsulin-associated enzymes are sequestered within the icosahedral shell through interactions between the shell's inner surface and a short localization sequence (Gly-Ser-Leu-Lys) appended to their C-termini.
source: The encapsulin-associated enzymes are sequestered within the icosahedral shell through interactions between the shell's inner surface and a short localization sequence (Gly-Ser-Leu-Lys) appended to their C-termini
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous structural and biochemical studies.

claim: The Myxococcus xanthus encapsulin acts as an 'iron-megastore' to protect bacteria from oxidative stress.
source: A recent study of the Myxococcus xanthus encapsulin showed that it sequesters a number of different EncFtn proteins and acts as an 'iron-megastore' to protect these bacteria from oxidative stress
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The M. xanthus encapsulin at 32 nm in diameter is capable of sequestering up to ten times more iron than classical ferritin nanocage (12 nm) and Dps complex (8 nm).
source: At 32 nm in diameter, it is much larger than other members of the ferritin superfamily, such as the 12 nm 24-subunit classical ferritin nanocage and the 8 nm 12-subunit Dps (DNA-binding protein from starved cells) complex (Grant et al., 1998; Andrews, 2010); and is thus capable of sequestering up to ten times more iron than these ferritins
evidence: This is based on size comparison and inference from volume calculations, supported by citations.

claim: EncFtn proteins have Glu-X-X-His metal coordination sites shared with ferritin family proteins.
source: The primary sequences of EncFtn proteins have Glu-X-X-His metal coordination sites, which are shared features of the ferritin family proteins
evidence: This is supported by sequence analysis and citation to ferritin literature.

claim: Secondary structure prediction identifies two major α-helical regions in EncFtn proteins, in contrast to four major α-helices in other ferritin superfamily members.
source: Secondary structure prediction identifies two major α-helical regions in these proteins; this is in contrast to other members of the ferritin superfamily, which have four major α-helices
evidence: This is supported by computational prediction and comparison with known ferritin structures.

claim: Rhodospirillum rubrum EncFtn protein shares 33% protein sequence identity with M. xanthus, 53% with T. maritima, and 29% with P. furiosus homologues.
source: The Rhodospirillum rubrum EncFtn protein (Rru_A0973) shares 33% protein sequence identity with the M. xanthus (MXAN_4464), 53% with the T. maritima (Tmari_0787), and 29% with the P. furiosus (PF1192) homologues.
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment analysis.

claim: The GXXH motifs are strictly conserved in R. rubrum, M. xanthus, T. maritima, and P. furiosus EncFtn homologues.
source: The GXXH motifs are strictly conserved in each of these species
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Supplementary file 1.

claim: Co-expression of R. rubrum encapsulin and EncFtn in E. coli leads to production of an icosahedral nanocompartment with encapsulated EncFtn.
source: Analysis by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) indicates that their co-expression leads to the production of an icosahedral nanocompartment with encapsulated EncFtn.
evidence: This is supported by TEM imaging data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The crystal structure of EncFtnsH shows it forms a decameric structure with an annular 'ring-doughnut' topology.
source: The crystal structure of a truncated hexahistidine-tagged variant of the EncFtn protein (EncFtnsH) shows that it forms a decameric structure with an annular 'ring-doughnut' topology
evidence: This is supported by X-ray crystallography data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The EncFtn decameric structure is distinct from the four-helical bundles of 24meric ferritins and dodecahedral DPS proteins.
source: which is distinct from the four-helical bundles of the 24meric ferritins (Lawson et al., 1991) and dodecahedral DPS proteins (Grant et al., 1998)
evidence: This is supported by structural comparison with known ferritin and DPS structures.

claim: A symmetrical iron bound ferroxidase center is formed between subunits in the EncFtn decamer.
source: We identify a symmetrical iron bound ferroxidase center (FOC) formed between subunits in the decamer
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic data showing iron coordination at the dimer interface (Figure 5).

claim: Additional metal-binding sites are present close to the center of the EncFtn ring and on the outer surface.
source: and additional metal-binding sites close to the center of the ring and on the outer surface
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic identification of metal ions at these locations (Figure 5).

claim: Metal-dependent assembly of EncFtn decamers is demonstrated by native PAGE, analytical gel-filtration, and native mass spectrometry.
source: We also demonstrate the metal-dependent assembly of EncFtn decamers using native PAGE, analytical gel-filtration, and native mass spectrometry.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2, 3, and 7.

claim: The conserved glutamic acid and histidine residues in the FOC influence protein assembly and activity.
source: Through site-directed mutagenesis we show that the conserved glutamic acid and histidine residues in the FOC influence protein assembly and activity.
evidence: This is supported by mutagenesis studies and biochemical assays shown in Figures 9-12.

claim: Recombinant R. rubrum encapsulin and EncFtn-Enc nanocompartments were purified by sucrose gradient ultracentrifugation from E. coli B834(DE3) grown in SeMet medium.
source: Recombinantly expressed encapsulin (Enc) and co-expressed EncFtn-Enc were purified by sucrose gradient ultracentrifugation from E. coli B834(DE3) grown in SeMet medium.
evidence: This is supported by the methods description and Figure 1A showing SDS-PAGE of purified proteins.

claim: R. rubrum encapsulin has a mean diameter of 24.6 nm with a standard deviation of 2.0 nm.
source: A model Gaussian nonlinear least square function was fitted to the data to obtain a mean diameter of 24.6 nm with a standard deviation of 2.0 nm for encapsulin
evidence: This is supported by TEM measurements and histogram analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Co-expressed EncFtn-Enc has a mean diameter of 23.9 nm with a standard deviation of 2.2 nm.
source: a mean value of 23.9 nm with a standard deviation of 2.2 nm for co-expressed EncFtn and encapsulin (EncFtn-Enc, black)
evidence: This is supported by TEM measurements and histogram analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Recombinant SeMet-labeled EncFtnsH produced with 1 mM Fe(NH4)2(SO4)2 elutes at approximately 73 ml on Superdex 200 16/60 column, corresponding to a molecular weight of around 130 kDa.
source: The peak around 73 ml corresponds to a molecular weight of around 130 kDa when compared to calibration standards; this is consistent with a decamer of EncFtnsH.
evidence: This is supported by size-exclusion chromatography data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Only the decamer peak of EncFtnsH contains significant amounts of iron as indicated by ICP-MS analysis.
source: Only the decamer peak contains significant amounts of iron as indicated by the ICP-MS analysis.
evidence: This is supported by ICP-MS data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: SEC-MALLS analysis assigns an average mass of 132 kDa to EncFtnsH decamer fractions and 13 kDa to monomer fractions.
source: SEC-MALLS analysis of EncFtnsH from decamer fractions and monomer fractions allows assignment of an average mass of 132 kDa to decamer fractions and 13 kDa to monomer fractions, consistent with decamer and monomer species
evidence: This is supported by SEC-MALLS data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Fe2+ facilitates the multimerization of EncFtnsH in vivo.
source: A higher proportion of decamer (peak between 65 and 75 ml) is seen in the sample purified from MM+Fe2+ compared to EncFtnsH-MM, indicating that Fe2+ facilitates the multimerization of EncFtnsH in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by gel filtration chromatography comparing samples grown with and without Fe2+ supplementation (Figure 3A).

claim: Fe(NH4)2(SO4)2 and FeSO4 induce the formation of EncFtnsH decamer from monomer in vitro.
source: Both Fe2+ salts tested induced the formation of decamer indicated by the peak between 1.2 and 1.6 ml.
evidence: This is supported by analytical gel-filtration data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Co2+ and Zn2+ induce the formation of decameric EncFtnsH.
source: Co2+ and Zn2+ induced the formation of the decameric form of EncFtnsH
evidence: This is supported by analytical gel-filtration data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mn2+, Mg2+ and Fe3+ do not significantly alter the oligomeric state of EncFtnsH.
source: while Mn2+, Mg2+ and Fe3+ did not significantly alter the oligomeric state of EncFtnsH
evidence: This is supported by analytical gel-filtration data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The EncFtnsH decamer is 7 nm in diameter and 4.5 nm thick.
source: The doughnut-like decamer is 7 nm in diameter and 4.5 nm thick.
evidence: This is supported by crystal structure analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The EncFtnsH monomer comprises three α-helices and a short 310 helix.
source: The monomer of EncFtnsH comprises three α-helices (α1, residues 11–42; α2, residues 48–76; α3, residues 82–103) and a short 310 helix (η1, residues 44–47)
evidence: This is supported by crystal structure analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The central hole in the EncFtnsH ring is 2.5 nm at its widest in the center and 1.5 nm at its narrowest point near the outer surface.
source: The central hole in the ring is 2.5 nm at its widest in the center of the complex, and 1.5 nm at its narrowest point near the outer surface
evidence: This is based on measurements from the crystal structure.

claim: The EncFtnsH structure contains a di-iron ferroxidase center coordinated by Glu32, Glu62, His65 and Tyr39.
source: Iron coordination within the FOC including residues Glu32, Glu62, His65 and Tyr39 from two chains.
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic data showing metal coordination (Figure 5B).

claim: A calcium ion is coordinated by Glu31 and Glu34 in the EncFtnsH structure.
source: The calcium ion coordinated by Glu31 and Glu34 adopts heptacoordinate geometry, with coordination distances of 2.5 Å between the metal ion and carboxylate oxygens of Glu31 and Glu34 (E31/34-site).
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic data (Figure 5C).

claim: Additional metal ions are coordinated by His57, Glu61 and Glu64 at the outer circumference of EncFtnsH.
source: A number of additional metal-ions were present at the outer circumference of at least one decamer in the asymmetric unit (Figure 5D). These ions are coordinated by His57, Glu61 and Glu64 from both chains in the FOC dimer
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic data (Figure 5D).

claim: The FOC residues in EncFtn are conserved with ferritin, with the exception of residues in the position equivalent to H65' in the second subunit.
source: Residues within the FOC are conserved between EncFtn and ferritin PmFtn, with the exception of residues in the position equivalent to H65' in the second subunit in the dimer (blue).
evidence: This is supported by structural alignment shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Native nanoelectrospray ionization mass spectrometry of EncFtnsH displays a charge state distribution consistent with monomer (13,194 Da) in the absence of iron.
source: nESI spectrum of iron-free EncFtnsH displays a charge state distribution consistent with EncFtnsH monomer (blue circles, 13,194 Da).
evidence: This is supported by native MS data shown in Figure 7A1.

claim: Addition of 100 µM and 300 µM Fe2+ to EncFtnsH results in the appearance of a charge state distribution consistent with a decameric assembly (132.6 kDa).
source: Addition of 100 µM (A2) and 300 µM (A3) Fe2+ results in the appearance of a second higher molecular weight charge state distribution consistent with a decameric assembly of EncFtnsH (green circles, 132.6 kDa).
evidence: This is supported by native MS data shown in Figure 7A2-A3.

claim: The EncFtnsH assembly binds between 10 and 15 Fe ions per decamer.
source: the observed m/z of the 24+ charge state indicates that the EncFtnsH assembly binds between 10 (green line, 5521.1 Th) and 15 Fe ions (blue line, 5532.4 Th) per decamer.
evidence: This is supported by native MS analysis of the 24+ charge state shown in Figure 7B.

claim: CID of the EncFtnsH decamer results in the appearance of a dimeric EncFtnsH subcomplex containing 0, 1, or 2 iron ions.
source: CID of the EncFtnsH decamer resulted in the appearance of a dimeric EncFtnsH subcomplex containing 0, 1, or 2 iron ions
evidence: This is supported by CID tandem MS data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: EncFtnsH shows no peroxidase activity when assayed with the substrate ortho-phenylenediamine.
source: Unlike the Dps family of ferritin-like proteins, EncFtn showed no peroxidase activity when assayed with the substrate ortho-phenylenediamine
evidence: This is supported by peroxidase assay data.

claim: EncFtnsH decamer displays ferroxidase activity comparable to apoferritin.
source: Apoferritin (10 μM monomer concentration) and EncFtnsH decamer fractions (20 μM monomer concentration, 10 μM FOC concentration) were incubated with 20 and 100 μM iron (2 and 10 times molar equivalent Fe2+ per FOC) and progress curves of the oxidation of Fe2+ to Fe3+ at 315 nm were recorded
evidence: This is supported by ferroxidase assay data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Encapsulin alone shows minimal ferroxidase activity.
source: Encapsulin and EncFtn-Enc complexes at 10 μM asymmetric unit concentration were incubated with Fe2+ at 20 and 100 μM and progress curves for iron oxidation at A315 were measured
evidence: This is inferred from Figure 8B showing encapsulin activity is similar to background oxidation.

claim: EncFtn-Enc nanocompartment displays ferroxidase activity.
source: Encapsulin and EncFtn-Enc complexes at 10 μM asymmetric unit concentration were incubated with Fe2+ at 20 and 100 μM and progress curves for iron oxidation at A315 were measured
evidence: This is supported by ferroxidase assay data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: EncFtnsH reaction mixture with Fe2+ shows formation of large, irregular electron-dense precipitates.
source: The EncFtnsH reaction mixture showed the formation of large, irregular electron-dense precipitates
evidence: This is supported by TEM imaging shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Addition of Fe2+ to EncFtn-Enc nanocompartment results in small, highly regular, electron dense particles of approximately 5 nm in diameter.
source: addition of Fe2+ to the EncFtn-Enc nanocompartment resulted in small, highly regular, electron dense particles of approximately 5 nm in diameter
evidence: This is supported by TEM imaging shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1C.

claim: EncFtnsH decamer binds a maximum of around 48 iron ions before excess iron induces protein precipitation.
source: In this assay, the EncFtnsH decamer binds a maximum of around 48 iron ions before excess iron induces protein precipitation.
evidence: This is supported by ferrozine assay data shown in Figure 8C and Table 5.

claim: The encapsulin shell protein can sequester about 2200 iron ions before significant protein loss occurs.
source: The encapsulin shell protein can sequester about 2200 iron ions before significant protein loss occurs
evidence: This is supported by ferrozine assay data shown in Figure 8C and Table 5.

claim: The reconstituted EncFtn-Enc nanocompartment sequestered about 4150 iron ions.
source: the reconstituted EncFtn-Enc nanocompartment sequestered about 4150 iron ions
evidence: This is supported by ferrozine assay data shown in Figure 8C and Table 5.

claim: Apoferritin sequesters approximately 570 iron ions in the ferrozine assay.
source: This latter result is significantly more than the apoferritin used in our assay, which sequesters approximately 570 iron ions in this assay
evidence: This is supported by ferrozine assay data shown in Figure 8C and Table 5.

claim: The E32A mutant of EncFtnsH elutes primarily as the decameric form with a small proportion of monomer on gel-filtration chromatography.
source: Gel-filtration chromatogram of the E32A mutant form of EncFtnsH resulted in an elution profile with a majority of the protein eluting as the decameric form of the protein and a small proportion of monomer.
evidence: This is supported by gel-filtration data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: The E62A mutant of EncFtnsH elutes as a single major decameric peak on gel-filtration chromatography.
source: Gel-filtration chromatograhy of the E62A mutant form of EncFtnsH resulted in an elution profile with a single major decameric peak.
evidence: This is supported by gel-filtration data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: The H65A mutant of EncFtnsH elutes as a single peak corresponding to the protein monomer on gel-filtration chromatography.
source: Gel-filtration chromatography of the H65A mutant form of EncFtnsH resulted in a single peak corresponding to the protein monomer.
evidence: This is supported by gel-filtration data shown in Figure 9C.

claim: E32A EncFtnsH displays charge states consistent with a decamer by native MS.
source: E32A EncFtnsH displays a charge states consistent with a decamer (green circles); a minor species, consistent with the monomer of E32A mutant is also observed (blue circles).
evidence: This is supported by native MS data shown in Figure 10B.

claim: E62A EncFtnsH displays charge states consistent with a decamer by native MS.
source: E62A EncFtnsH displays charge states consistent with a decamer (green circles).
evidence: This is supported by native MS data shown in Figure 10C.

claim: H65A EncFtnsH displays charge states consistent with both monomer and dimer by native MS.
source: H65A EncFtnsH displays charge states consistent with both monomer (blue circles) and dimer (purple circles).
evidence: This is supported by native MS data shown in Figure 10D.

claim: The E32A, E62A and H65A mutants of EncFtnsH are essentially isomorphous to the wild-type structure in crystal packing.
source: The crystal packing of all of the mutants in this study is essentially isomorphous to the EncFtnsH structure.
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic analysis with RMSDCα of less than 0.2 Å.

claim: All EncFtnsH mutants display the same decameric arrangement in crystals as the wild-type structure.
source: All of the mutants display the same decameric arrangement in the crystals as the EncFtnsH structure
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic analysis.

claim: The E32A mutant has no coordinated metal ions in the FOC region.
source: Of the mutants, only H65A has any coordinated metal ions, which appear to be calcium ions from the crystallization condition.
evidence: This is inferred from Figure 11 and Figure 11—figure supplement 1 showing no metal density in E32A FOC.

claim: The E62A mutant has a single coordinated calcium ion in the FOC region.
source: The single coordinated calcium ion is shown as a grey sphere.
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic data shown in Figure 11—figure supplement 2.

claim: The H65A mutant has coordinated calcium ions in the FOC region.
source: Of the mutants, only H65A has any coordinated metal ions, which appear to be calcium ions from the crystallization condition.
evidence: This is supported by crystallographic data shown in Figure 11 and Figure 11—figure supplement 3.

claim: The E62A mutant significantly abrogates ferroxidase activity.
source: The FOC mutants showed reduced ferroxidase activity to varied extents, among which E62A significantly abrogated the ferroxidase activity.
evidence: This is supported by ferroxidase assay data shown in Figure 12.

claim: The E32A and H65A mutants show reduced but not abolished ferroxidase activity.
source: The FOC mutants showed reduced ferroxidase activity to varied extents
evidence: This is inferred from Figure 12 showing E32A and H65A retain partial activity compared to E62A.

claim: EncFtn family proteins form a distinct clade within the ferritin superfamily based on phylogenetic analysis.
source: Phylogenetic analysis of the ferritin superfamily based on the four-helix bundle shows that the EncFtn family forms a distinct clade
evidence: This is supported by phylogenetic tree analysis shown in Figure 13.

claim: The central ring of EncFtn corresponds to the external surface of classical ferritin.
source: A structural alignment of the FOC of EncFtn with the classical ferritin PmFtn shows that the central ring of EncFtn corresponds to the external surface of ferritin
evidence: This is supported by structural alignment analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The outer circumference of EncFtn is congruent with the inner mineralization surface of ferritin.
source: while the outer circumference of EncFtn is congruent with the inner mineralization surface of ferritin
evidence: This is supported by structural alignment analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The ferroxidase center of EncFtn faces in the opposite direction relative to classical ferritins.
source: This overlay highlights the fact that the ferroxidase center of EncFtn faces in the opposite direction relative to the classical ferritins and is essentially inside out regarding iron storage space
evidence: This is based on structural comparison and inference from the alignment.

claim: The calcium ion coordinated by Glu31 and Glu34 acts as an entry site to channel metal ions into the FOC.
source: Furthermore, the position of the calcium ion coordinated by Glu31 and Glu34 seen in the EncFtnsH structure suggests an entry site to channel metal ions into the FOC; we propose that this site binds hydrated iron ions in vivo and acts as a selectivity filter and gate for the FOC
evidence: This is a proposal based on structural data and inference about function.

claim: His57, Glu61 and Glu64 on the outer circumference of EncFtn may function as the exit portal and mineralization site.
source: The constellation of charged residues on the outer circumference of EncFtn (His57, Glu61 and Glu64) could function in the same way as the residues lining the mineralization surface within the classical ferritin nanocage (Le Brun et al., 2010), and given their proximity to the FOC these sites may be the exit portal and mineralization site
evidence: This is a proposal based on structural data, comparison with ferritin, and speculation about function.

claim: EncFtn family proteins are not capable of storing iron minerals due to the absence of an enclosed compartment in their structure.
source: The absolute requirement for the spatial separation of oxidation and mineralization in ferritins suggests that the EncFtn family proteins are not capable of storing iron minerals due to the absence of an enclosed compartment in their structure
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and inference from ferritin function requirements.

claim: Mineralization of iron occurs within the cavity of the encapsulin shell.
source: While EncFtn does not store iron itself, its association with the encapsulin nanocage suggests that mineralization occurs within the cavity of the encapsulin shell
evidence: This is based on inference from the structural arrangement and biochemical data.

claim: The central channel of EncFtnsH is positioned directly above the pore in the encapsulin pentamer axis when docked to the encapsulin shell.
source: Alignment of EncFtnsH with 3DKT positions the central channel directly above the pore in the 3DKT pentamer axis
evidence: This is based on structural modeling and alignment shown in Figure 14A.

claim: The lumen of the encapsulin nanocompartment is considerably larger than the interior of ferritin.
source: The lumen of the encapsulin nanocompartment is considerably larger than the interior of ferritin (shown in orange behind the encapsulin for reference) and thus allows the storage of significantly more iron.
evidence: This is based on structural comparison shown in Figure 14B.

claim: Fe2+ must pass through the encapsulin shell to access the first metal binding site within the central channel of EncFtnsH prior to oxidation within the FOC.
source: As EncFtn is unable to mineralize iron on its surface directly, Fe2+ must pass through the encapsulin shell to access the first metal binding site within the central channel of EncFtnsH (entry site) prior to oxidation within the FOC
evidence: This is a proposed model based on structural and biochemical data shown in Figure 14C.

claim: Fe3+ is released to the outer surface of EncFtn where it can be mineralized within the lumen of the encapsulin cage.
source: and release as Fe3+ to the outer surface of the protein where it can be mineralized within the lumen of the encapsulin cage
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on structural and biochemical data shown in Figure 14C.

claim: The encapsulin shell protein has a negatively charged pore positioned to allow passage of Fe2+ into the encapsulin.
source: The crystal structure of the T. maritima encapsulin shell protein has a negatively charged pore positioned to allow the passage of Fe2+ into the encapsulin
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the T. maritima encapsulin and inference about function.

claim: The five metal-binding sites on the interior of the EncFtn ring may select for Fe2+ ion and direct it towards their cognate FOCs.
source: The five metal-binding sites on the interior of the ring (Glu31/34-sites) may select for the Fe2+ ion and direct it towards their cognate FOCs.
evidence: This is a proposal based on structural data and speculation about function.

claim: The oxidation of Fe2+ to Fe3+ occurs within the FOC according to the model postulated by Honarmand Ebrahimi et al. (2012).
source: We propose that the oxidation of Fe2+ to Fe3+ occurs within the FOC according to the model postulated by (Honarmand Ebrahimi et al., 2012)
evidence: This is a proposal based on citation to a previous mechanistic model.

claim: The FOC acts as a substrate site through which iron passes and is released onto weakly coordinating sites at the outer circumference of the protein.
source: in which the FOC acts as a substrate site through which iron passes and is released on to weakly coordinating sites at the outer circumference of the protein (His57, Glu61 and Glu64)
evidence: This is part of the proposed mechanism based on structural data and speculation.

claim: Fe3+ forms ferrihydrite minerals which can be deposited within the lumen of the encapsulin nanocompartment.
source: where it is able to form ferrihydrite minerals which can be safely deposited within the lumen of the encapsulin nanocompartment
evidence: This is part of the proposed mechanism based on biochemical data and inference.
